body: jj angle, expanded: in a colocated jj repo everything should work today unmodified, since the git backend stores real refs and objects. Two things to verify before claiming it: (1) jj's GC of hidden/abandoned commits respects git ref reachability, so retention parents on refs/threads/data should protect anchored commits — confirm. (2) jj-heavy workflows rewrite constantly, so most threads will live in relocated/fuzzy/outdated states — good stress test for the ladder. The real prize is this change_id field: a jj change ID (or Gerrit Change-Id) is a rebase-stable identity, so a thread could follow a logical change across rewrites instead of pinning to a dead commit and relying on snippet matching. Needs design: where does the reader resolve change-id -> current commit without jj installed?
